audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 and late-game text told you to hold your R to 'cancel his spin engage'. Zaahen's R has no crowd control at all.
audit.why: Riot's text: he rises, stabs downward, damages and heals for a portion of the damage dealt. It cannot interrupt Cyclone. Treating it as an interrupt loses the fight and the 110-second cooldown together.
audit.corrected: spikes[1].text and late rewritten to hold R for after the spin, as damage and healing.

audit.whatIsWrong: Zaahen's W was called 'Ominous Return sustain' in mid and spikes[3] — his W does damage and pulls, with no healing anywhere in its text. His healing is on Q. Wukong's Crushing Blow auto-attack reset was never given as the trade tell, and the Q recast knock-up as an answer to his dash-in was absent.
audit.why: The double slash on Q is what heals him, and the recast turns the next attack into a knock-up — that is the tool that answers Nimbus Strike, not the W. Wukong's Q is an auto reset, so the wind-up rather than the cast is the cue to step back (flagged in missingInteractions).
audit.corrected: mid, spikes[3].text, dosFull[0..2].d, dontsFull[0..2].d and breakdown.cooldowns rewritten with the pull's 850 range, the Q heal and recast, and the reset tell.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns used the placeholder 'Your committal tool' and gave no numbers.
audit.why: The concrete windows available from the data are Zaahen's own: Q 10s and E 10s at rank 1, W 850 range.
audit.corrected: Rewritten. No Wukong cooldowns were written because the brief's enemyKit is null — see unverified.

edits.before: His Cyclone (R) is a knock-up-and-spin ult that turns a decent trade into a kill if his jungler collapses. Hold your R Final Retribution as an anti-engage rather than opening with it, and stand away from your minions so the spin can't chain-lift you into tower.
edits.after: His Cyclone (R) is a knock-up-and-spin ult that turns a decent trade into a kill if his jungler collapses. Hold your R for after the spin, as damage and healing rather than an interrupt — it has no CC — and stand clear of your minions so the lift cannot chain you.

edits.before: This is Wukong's window and the reason the timeline is his: from level 3 his E-Q-W combo shreds your armour and the clone eats your telegraphed E Golden Onslaught, and at 6 his Cyclone converts any trade you lose into a death. Play reactive — poke with Q, keep W Ominous Return sustain topped, and never dash first into an untested clone.
edits.after: This is Wukong's window and the reason the timeline is his: from level 3 his E-Q-W combo shreds your armour and the clone eats your telegraphed E dash, and at 6 his Cyclone converts any trade you lose into a death. Play reactive — poke with Q, whose double slash heals you back, and never dash first into an untested clone.

edits.before: With items Wukong out-duels you in the sidelane and his clone plus Cyclone make him a slippery pick threat in fights. Don't chase — win by grouping, forcing your team onto the clone, and holding R Final Retribution to cancel his spin engage.
edits.after: With items Wukong out-duels you in the sidelane and his clone plus Cyclone make him a slippery pick threat in fights. Don't chase — win by grouping, forcing your team onto the clone, and saving R for after his spin; it heals, it does not interrupt.

edits.before: Two items in, Wukong stays ahead: his clone makes your telegraphed E engages a coin-flip and Cyclone is a reliable teamfight disengage/pick. Play around your W Ominous Return sustain and let your team eat the clone before you commit.
edits.after: Two items in, Wukong stays ahead: his clone makes your telegraphed E dash a coin-flip and Cyclone is a reliable teamfight disengage and pick. Play around the heal on your Q double slash, and let your team eat the clone before you commit.

edits.before: His engage dash. Combo after it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: His engage dash. Punish the landing — your W pull reaches 850 units.

edits.before: Probe Wukong's pattern early, then commit your full combo only on his key cooldown — bank knowledge before blood.
edits.after: The clone eats exactly one commit — make it eat an auto, never your E dash or your 110-second ultimate.

edits.before: Wukong wastes Nimbus Strike — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Crushing Blow is an auto reset — the wind-up is the cue, not the cast.

edits.before: That is Wukong's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: Your E dash is 10s at rank 1 — spend it on the clone and you fight him without it.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Q recast knocks him up — hold it for his dash-in, not the wave.

edits.before: Coin-flipping into an unknown matchup — respect what you have not seen until you have seen it twice.
edits.after: His Q shreds armour, so more armour is not the answer — break the trade after his first two autos.

edits.before: - Wukong Nimbus Strike: matchup-defining — His engage dash. Combo after it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Wukong Nimbus Strike: his engage dash — punish the landing with your 850-range W pull. - Crushing Blow: an auto reset; the wind-up is the tell. - Your Q: 10s at rank 1, recast knocks up. - Your R: kill windows only.

notes: The brief's enemyKit is null for Wukong, so no Wukong cooldown numbers were written anywhere — every concrete number in these edits comes from Zaahen's own kit. Zaahen's W was described as a sustain tool ('Ominous Return sustain') in two places; his W damages and pulls, and the healing is on Q. His R was described as an interrupt; it has no CC.
